label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 5

hints.title: Use the symmetry to label the gaps
hints.body: First find the square side. Reflect a marked corner length in each symmetry line to express the remaining side gaps using x.
hints.recap: Reflection symmetry gives equal corresponding lengths.
hints.pitfall: The rectangle is tilted; its side lengths are not the gaps along the square edges.
hints.pause: Label all the square-edge segments before calculating an area.

recall.reminder: Reflection symmetry gives equal corresponding lengths.

hints.title: Remove the corner pieces
hints.body: Find the area of each right triangle outside the rectangle and subtract their total from the square area.
hints.recap: An inscribed area can be found as the outer area minus the surrounding pieces.
hints.pitfall: Each triangle area has a factor one half.
hints.pause: Set your rectangle-area expression equal to the given area.

recall.reminder: An inscribed area can be found as the outer area minus the surrounding pieces.

hints.title: Retain the geometric roots
hints.body: Solve the resulting quadratic, then check which roots lie between the endpoints of the square side.
hints.recap: A quadratic can have two geometrically valid roots.
hints.pitfall: The question requests the largest permitted x, not an arbitrary quadratic root.
hints.pause: Check both roots and select the requested one.

recall.reminder: A quadratic can have two geometrically valid roots.

solution:
1. Label the square. Its side is 40/4=10. Reflection in each diagonal shows MR=MU=OS=OT=x and NR=NS=PT=PU=10−x.

2. Subtract the corners. The four corner triangles are right-angled. Two have legs x and two have legs 10−x, so the rectangle area is 100−x2−(10−x)2=2x(10−x).

3. Use the given area. 2x(10−x)=20 gives x2−10x+10=0, hence x=5±15. Both lie strictly between 0 and 10. The larger is 5+15. Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Subtract corner triangles from an enclosing square and select the larger feasible root
